notes: A HARD CALL, NOT A FINDING. The commune, an outside party, takes on the father's dotal burden for a price fixed in advance. The 1425 terms were 100 florins in cash for seven and a half or fifteen years, yielding 250 or 500 florins (Molho 30), so that 'a father's material burden shifted to the polity' (Molho 32). After the reform of 23 April 1433, 'investors preferred to pay the equivalent of a premium to ensure the security of their capital' (Molho 43), and Molho calls the deposit 'something akin to betting on people's life-expectancy' and 'primitive insurance policies' (Molho 34). The commune keeps what the dead forfeit and treats it as its own: the law of 29 March 1452 took credits from the dowry account on the ground that 'the credits of this account are in great excess because of the girls who have already died and of those who, in all likelihood, will die before payment' (Molho 49; English translation only, original not printed in the source). No depositor's payout depends on another depositor's fate: the dowry is fixed by deposit and term. ALTERNATIVES, stated fairly. (a) pooling: the forfeits of girls who die finance the yield paid to girls who marry, and Molho computes the government's real cost of financing claims as reduced by the girls lost to death or the convent (Molho 45); the cross-subsidy among depositors is real, but it runs through the commune's price and residual, not through a mutual of stakeholders with no outsider. (b) allocation: the enactment assigns the peril of the girl's death to the depositor by rule (see RB1). SPLIT TEST: the refund of capital on death of 23 April 1433, its reversal of 24 May 1434 and its restoration in January 1435/6 (Molho 34-35) change what the premium buys, not who stands behind the aggregate; a variant, no split. Harris's three values were drawn for maritime perils and fit a contingent claim on a commune badly; the value is the least wrong of three. Prior (pooling, low) falsified toward spreading, at low confidence. MS RULING 2026-10-15: spreading kept; the row is therefore outside the risk-pooling view (filter MC1 = pooling) by design. Confidence raised from low (as coded) to medium by MS ruling the same day, on the argument that no member's payout depends on another member's fate and the residual sits with the commune.

Eligibility attaches to the girl and is defined by the commune's dominion. 1425: 'Quod cuicunque, undecunque et cuiuscunque conditionis et status existenti liceat sub nomine et pro dote cuiuscunque puelle seu filie habilis ad acquirendum de creditis montium dicti comunis . . .' (PR 114, 23 February 1424/5; Molho 81 n. 3). 1434: 'Quelibet puella tam de civitate, comitatu vel districtu Florentie quam de quocumque loco in quo comune Florentie preheminentiam vel custodiam haberet intelligatur esse et sit habilis . . . ad predicta' (PR 125, 24 May 1434; Molho 82 n. 5). Without special dispensation foreigners had no access (Molho 81). The depositor is unrestricted by the 1425 clause (cuicunque, undecunque); the ground of belonging is the beneficiary's standing as a subject able to hold Monte credits. ALTERNATIVE: contract, membership being made by the deposit; rejected because the deposit is the act of joining and the dominion is the ground of eligibility. VARIANTS, no split, the value holding throughout: 'qualunche originario cittadino sopportante in qualunche modo le graveçce nella città di Firençe' (PR 152, 17 January 1461/2; Molho 82 n. 6), the word originario struck out in 1463 (Molho 82 n. 7); separate ceilings for girls of the contado and distretto from 21 March 1451/2 (Molho 52, 111); a certificate of tax standing required from 30 April 1477 (Molho 83 n. 10). Prior (contract, low) falsified.

Closed to a defined class from the start, and numerically capped from the 1470s. Closure: only a girl 'habilis ad acquirendum de creditis montium' (PR 114, 1424/5; Molho 81 n. 3), foreigners only by special enactment (Molho 81). Entry by certificate: 'Et chi vorrà fare tali dote . . . debba . . . haver dato al notaio overo cancelliere del monte il nome della fanciulla et la quantità vorrà fare et portato la fede che la fanciulla è netta di specchio nel modo sopradetto . . . et altrimenti non gli sia acceptata né facta' (Cento 1, 30 April 1477; Molho 83 n. 10). Numerical limb: from the reforms of 1471/2 a ceiling, the ritratto, on the total matured value of all dowries deposited in a given year (Molho 53). SPLIT TEST: the ritratto adds a numerical limb to a closure that already held, so the value is 1 before and after; a variant, no split. Boys' accounts, created by the second bill of 1424/5 and limited to orphans by 27 May 1457 (Molho 30, 53), sit inside the fund and do not move the cell. Prior (1, low) held.

'Quod cuicunque . . . liceat sub nomine et pro dote cuiuscunque puelle . . .' (PR 114, 23 February 1424/5; Molho 81 n. 3): it is permitted, not required. Behaviour bears the clause out: 'only two fathers came forth to make deposits in 1425, and none did during the next three years' (Molho 32), and the terms were sweetened again and again to draw depositors in (Molho 32-35). The compulsory deposit in Monte credits from March 1440/1 (Molho 37) governs the medium of a voluntary deposit, not participation. The special gabella on depositors of January 1530/1, with penalties of a quarter to half of the matured dowry (Molho 77), is dated 16 January 1531 modern style, outside 1425-1530, and taxes existing accounts rather than compelling entry. No split. Prior (voluntary, high) held; the house cap holds the cell at medium.

source_ref: Molho 1994, 30, 37, 83 n. 11; Kirshner and Molho 1978, 409, 411; Morrison, Kirshner and Molho 1985, 529
notes: A single payment at opening buys a dowry fixed for a fixed term. A surviving certificate of 1477 (Monte 1344): 'Simone di Matteo di Piero Cini k[amarling]o al monte riceve dalla Checca . . . figliuola di Simone d'Ubertino di Gherardo Risaliti . . . nata a dì 18 di giugnio 1471 f. 72 larghi per fare f. 400 di dota . . . chome apare a libro nero primo c. 165, cioè per anni quindici' (Molho 83 n. 11). The model terms have the same shape: 100 florins for seven and a half or fifteen years in 1425 (Molho 30); in April 1433, 60 florins for five, seven and a half, eleven or fifteen years, yielding 140, 250, 365 or 500 florins (Kirshner and Molho 1978, 409, Table 1). VARIANTS, no split: 'More than one deposit was made for a number of girls' (Morrison, Kirshner and Molho 1985, 529), each a lump; deposits in Monte credits at market value, invited from February 1439/40 and compulsory from March 1440/1 (Molho 37; Kirshner and Molho 1978, 411, give March 24, 1441). One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (ex-ante-lump, high) held; cap medium.

The depositor chooses the dowry he buys and pays for it at a rate fixed by the term: 'investors could choose to deposit as much or as little as they wished' (Molho 30); 'neither a minimum nor a maximum was fixed for the sum one might deposit' (Kirshner and Molho 1978, 406); one model deposit per term, scaled to the dowry (Kirshner and Molho 1978, 409, Table 1). The stake is the matured dowry claimed, and the contribution is that stake times the term's rate. Not equal (there is no unit deposit) and not proportional-to-capacity (nothing grades the deposit by wealth or tax assessment). FIT: the vocabulary has no value for a contribution the member chooses; proportional-to-stake is the nearest true one, flagged. VARIANTS, no split: rates changed repeatedly (Molho 32-35); premiums for noncitizens raised by 20 to 30 percent (Molho 111); from 1458 the deposit pegged to the market price of Monte credits (Molho 53), so that under the scale of 14 June 1459 credits worth 16 florins in cash matured to 100 florins in fifteen years (Molho 55 n. 82); ceilings on the matured dowry from 21 March 1451/2 (Molho 52). Each changes the rate, not the basis. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (proportional-to-stake, low) held; raised to medium because the sources state the deposit-to-dowry relation outright.

Inapplicable: the contribution is a single sum paid before the account exists, so no contribution is ever outstanding and none can be compelled. 'et altrimenti non gli sia acceptata né facta' (Cento 1, 30 April 1477; Molho 1994, 83 n. 10): without payment there is no account. No instalment deposit is recorded in the sources read. The special gabella of January 1530/1 with its penalties (Molho 1994, 77) is a tax on depositors, dated 16 January 1531 modern style and outside the period; it would bear on CN3 only if read as a contribution. Inapplicability runs back to CN1 = ex-ante-lump and agrees with it. Prior (.NA, low) held.

Two hazards fall on the girls and their claims. The girl's death is idiosyncratic in ordinary years and synchronised in epidemics: 'Annual death rates of girls enrolled in the Dowry Fund increased by 5 to 10 times in each of these periods' (the epidemics of 1430, 1437-38, 1449-50, 1478-79 and 1527-31), and 'Recurrent epidemics accounted for 38 per cent of the total mortality experienced by girls enrolled in the Dowry Fund' (Morrison, Kirshner and Molho 1985, 528). The commune's capacity to pay is perfectly covariate across claimants: eight monthly instalments ordered 16 August 1441 (Molho 38), one-third in cash in 1472 and one-fifth from 1475 (Molho 66, 68), 'chronic arrears' (Molho 68). One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. The epidemiological article is co-authored by Kirshner and Molho from the same registers. No split: both components hold through the period, the covariate fiscal one sharpening after 1472. Prior (mixed, medium) held.

A STRUCTURAL HALF. The peril itself, a daughter's death, does not respond to the cover; the claim does. (a) Timing: in a sample of 76 marriages, 47 (61.84 percent) took place within six months of the deposit's maturity and 39 (51.31 percent) within three months (Kirshner and Molho 1978, 419); on Klapisch-Zuber's reading, which Kirshner calls insightful, the consummation requirement 'spurred Florentine husbands to perform their conjugal duty pronto in order to collect the Monte dowry' (Kirshner 2015, 100). (b) False claims: 'non aveva consumato il matrimonio quando ebe detta dote per cui il padre fu condemnato in fiorini 500' (MC 3735, 3v; Kirshner 2015, 298 n. 53); Vannuccio di Arriguccio's father-in-law fined 500 florins in 1459 (Kirshner 2015, 101). (c) Selection: deposits moved from daughters judged unfit for marriage to their sisters (Molho 61-62), and Molho suspects fathers understated their daughters' ages (Molho 359-360). The census's P reading, the claim responding to the cover, is the one taken. ALTERNATIVES: .NR, since the sources never frame responsiveness as such; or 0, on the peril alone. No split. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (.NR) falsified toward P, at low.

The pool pays the matured dowry to the husband of an enrolled girl who has married and consummated, irrespective of any loss. Marriage is the outcome hoped for, and the sum is fixed by deposit and term (Molho 30). It is financed in part by what the families of girls who die forfeit (Molho 31, 45), so it concentrates a fixed promise onto the girls who survive and marry. FIT: the vocabulary glosses individual-draw as receipt 'by rotation, lot or auction'; this draw is by event, which no value names. ALTERNATIVE, stated fairly: individual-indemnity. The payment relieves the father's dotal obligation; the enactment pays 'pro restitutione quantitatis solute pro dote et usque in quantitatem receptam pro dote talis puelle' (PR 114; Molho 31 n. 16); and the husband had to show a dowry promised at least equal to the matured value (Molho 32). Rejected because a dowry is an outlay chosen at a life event, not a realised loss, and the payout is not measured by it. VARIANTS, no split: the capital refunded on the girl's death from 23 April 1433 and on her profession as a nun from 15 May 1437 (Molho 34-35); these refunds return the depositor's own principal and add no second output. Prior (individual-draw, low) held.

source_ref: Molho 1994, 30, 31 n. 16, 34-35; Kirshner 2015, 96; Kirshner and Molho 1978, 408, 409 n. 16
notes: '. . . postquam vir consumaverit matrimonium et non ante' (PR 114, 23 February 1424/5; Molho 31 n. 16; Kirshner 2015, 96), once the term has run (Molho 30). LOCUS: the trigger is the enrolled girl's own marriage; the payee is her husband. VARIANTS, no split: the deposit refunded on the girl's death from 23 April 1433, 'a year and a day after her death', to her father or brothers (Molho 34; Kirshner and Molho 1978, 408), after two years from 20 November 1436 (Molho 35); refunded on monastic profession from 15 May 1437: '. . . tunc statim facta professione legitime dicta puella professa habeatur et reputetur tamquam vere mortua ad contenta dumtaxat in presenti provisione' (PR 128; Kirshner and Molho 1978, 409 n. 16). Every trigger is a life event. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (life-event, high) held; cap medium.

NO FITTING VALUE. Nothing is allocated among eligible claimants: the trigger (PY1) designates the payee, and deposit and term fix the sum (Molho 30; Kirshner and Molho 1978, 409, Table 1). It is not rotation, lot, auction or need-assessment. House practice also uses indemnity for a payee fixed by the trigger, but PY0 here is a draw irrespective of loss, and indemnity would contradict it. The annual ritratto from 1471/2 (Molho 53) rations entry, not the draw. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (.NR, no fit) held.

Capped independently of what the marriage cost. The sum is fixed when the deposit is made, 'f. 72 larghi per fare f. 400 di dota . . . cioè per anni quindici' (Monte 1344, 1477; Molho 83 n. 11), and a girl who married after the term brought 'only the sum originally established, with no additional interest for the extra time' (Molho 30). VARIANTS, no split: ceilings on the matured value from 21 March 1451/2, of 1,200 florins for citizens' legitimate daughters, 500 for their illegitimate daughters, 400 for legitimate daughters of contadini and distrettuali and 50 for foundlings of the Innocenti (Molho 52), lowered for citizens' daughters to 1,000 florins in 1458/9 and to 800 fiorini larghi in January 1471/2 (Molho 52); the cash share of a payment cut to one-fifth from 1475 and to 20 percent from November 1478 (Molho 68-69). A second cap on a capped draw does not change the value. Prior (1, medium) held.

When the fund could not pay, every claimant took the same fraction. Eight monthly instalments were ordered on 16 August 1441 (Molho 38), and monthly instalments again in February 1443/4; from 18 August 1446 payment was in Monte credits issued at a discount of 18 percent and redeemed in cash at 16 percent (Molho 47); in 1472 one-third of every dowry was paid in cash and two-thirds in credits at a discount of 22 percent (Molho 66); from 1475 one-fifth in cash (Molho 66, 68); from November 1478, 20 percent in cash and 80 percent inscribed at face value in the Monte dei sette per cento at 7 percent (Molho 69); the cash share rose to 25 percent in 1482 and 33 percent in February 1507/8 (Molho 71). The rule is a uniform proportional deferral or haircut across claimants: pro-rata. QUALIFIED: Molho also writes that 'until 1478, when the Fund was profoundly transformed, mature dowries were paid in full, more or less promptly' (Molho 45), so before 1472 the burden was mostly delay, and Molho names the commune's other course, supplementing the payments of matured dowries with additional appropriations (Molho 46). SPLIT TEST, considered and not proposed: before 16 August 1441 the sources record no shortfall and no rule. The enactment pays 'de quacunque pecunia' (Molho 31 n. 16) and 'made no provision for payment of matured dowries' (Molho 31); the earlier phase is unrecorded, not a different value. Prior (.NR before the crisis, pro-rata after, low) held in substance.

AN OBSERVED ABSENCE. Depositors hold a fixed claim and no claim on surplus, and the commune treated the surplus left by the dead as its own and took it. By the law of 29 March 1452, 300,000 florins of credits were drawn from the creditum puellarum maritandarum on the ground that 'the credits of this account are in great excess because of the girls who have already died and of those who, in all likelihood, will die before payment' (Molho 49; English translation, original not printed in the source); by the law of 22 December 1456, 40,000 florins were diverted to military expenses (Molho 49); Girolamo Machiavelli's warning in January 1455/6 was not heeded (Molho 49). No split: the inscription of unpaid balances in the 7 percent fund in 1478 (Molho 69) gives claimants interest, not a share of surplus. Prior (0, medium) held.

Not addressed. No source read shows a depositor or husband pursued for the fund's losses beyond what he paid in. The fines on husbands for false consummation (Kirshner 2015, 101) and for failing to present the confessio dotis (Molho 57-58) are penalties for misconduct, not liability for the pool. The husband's duty to restore the dowry runs to his wife under dotal law (Kirshner 2015, 102-108), not to the fund. The special gabella of January 1530/1, with penalties of a quarter to half of the matured dowry (Molho 77), falls on 16 January 1531 modern style, outside the period, and is a tax. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (.NR) held.

source_ref: Kirshner 2015, 96, 101-102, 298 n. 54; Molho 1994, 356 n. 14, 358-359; Morrison, Kirshner and Molho 1985, 529
notes: The Monte officials decided each payment on declarations and instruments laid before them. 'deliberaverunt quod Baldus supradictus habeat dotem suam, recepta fide quod dictus Baldus consumavit dictum matrimonium' (NA 6136, 30r, May 1452; Kirshner 2015, 102 and 298 n. 54). 'Non pagare se gli ufficiali non la veggono' (Monte 3734, f. 182r; Molho 356 n. 14). Every payment of a matured dowry or of capital returned 'was taken up and voted on individually' (Molho 359). The evidence before them: oral declarations by the husband and the bride's father and brothers (Kirshner 2015, 96); a statement sworn before a notary when the officials doubted (Kirshner 2015, 101-102); written attestation from husbands of the contado and distretto, the earliest reference February 1454 (Kirshner 2015, 102); and deaths reported by a relative or cleric and, if questioned, certified by the sworn testimony of four witnesses, within two months under a provision of February 1447 (Morrison, Kirshner and Molho 1985, 529). ALTERNATIVE: documentary, the notarial instruments being the evidentiary base; rejected because the decisive act the sources record is the officials' deliberation. DISAGREEMENT WITHIN THE WITNESS: Kirshner places the oral declarations before the Monte officials (96); Molho places them before the officials of the gabella dei contratti (358). Variants by residence, no split. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (documentary, low) falsified toward official-adjudication.

Two objects are verified before payment. Occurrence: that the enrolled girl married and the marriage was consummated ('postquam vir consumaverit matrimonium et non ante', PR 114; Molho 31 n. 16). Compliance: 'in quantum fuerit consummatum matrimonium et dos confessata et soluta ghabella. Loysius pater dicte Costantie consensit' (MC 1124, 4v; Kirshner 2015, 306 n. 111), that is, the confessio dotis executed, the contract tax paid and the father's consent given; also the husband's standing as a taxpayer (Kirshner 2015, 95-96) and, where the officials acted in place of the bride's father, security for restoring the dowry under a law of 1441 (Kirshner 2015, 112). SPLIT TEST: the 1425 clause names consummation only. Kirshner states the full conditions in the context of the 1433 terms (94-95), and no payment before 1433 appears in the sources read, the first deposits of 1425 having run seven and a half or fifteen years (Molho 30, 32). No split proposed. DATING DISAGREEMENT within the witness on the law of 1441, PR 132, ff. 6v-9r: 24 March 1440/1 (Molho 37 n. 37), March 24, 1441 (Kirshner and Molho 1978, 411), 24 Mar. 1441/2 (Kirshner 2015, 308 n. 117); the first two agree on 1441 modern style. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (loss-occurrence or mixed, low) held on its second limb.

The enactment binds communal officers: 'Officiales et camerarii montis . . . teneantur et debeant . . . de quacunque pecunia . . . restituere . . . atque solvere pro dote . . .' (PR 114, 23 February 1424/5; Molho 31 n. 16). Every term was set by the legislative councils and the Monte's officials and reformers (Molho 30-77), and every payment by the officials' deliberation (Kirshner 2015, 298 n. 54). The depositors had no organ. No split: the Thirty Reformers of 1458 and the reorganisation of November 1478 (Molho 53, 68) change which communal body decides, not the mode. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (external-administered, high) held; cap medium.

A standing fund with continuous enrolment and no terminal date: 'dowry deposits were accepted until the late 1540s' (Molho 70), and 'It appears that no decree was formally enacted to end its operations' (Molho 77). Each deposit has a term; the pool does not. The new accounts puellarum maritandarum opened in 1452 and 1458 (Molho 38) and the annual ritratto from 1471/2 (Molho 53) are bookkeeping and rationing cohorts, not cycles liquidated on completion. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Morrison, Kirshner and Molho 1985, 529 ('quite active until 1530') agree and are not independent. Prior (open-ended, high) held; cap medium.
Inapplicable where DR1 is open-ended. Propagated .NA under the vocabulary's applicability rule.

The depositor, as capital provider, bears the peril of the girl's death in every phase; what changes is how much he loses. 1425: if the girl died or never married 'it reverted to the Commune' (Molho 30), so that 'an investor suffered a substantial loss by forfeiting not only the possible returns on his investment but by losing all capital as well' (Molho 31). From 23 April 1433 the deposit was repaid to her father or brothers a year and a day after her death; the gain was still forfeited, and so was the capital where neither survived (Molho 34). Reversed by the law of 24 May 1434, restored in January 1435/6, and the repayment deferred to two years from 20 November 1436 (Molho 34-35); fictive fathers or brothers could be nominated from April 1446 (Molho 111); no refund for noncitizen girls from 4 February 1455/6 to 18 June 1463, and again from 10 January 1471/2 (Molho 111-112). The commune bears no loss on a death; it gains. SPLIT TEST: every phase gives capital-provider, so these are variants of magnitude, not a split. LOCATOR: the vocabulary pairs capital and labour providers; the depositor maps cleanly onto capital-provider, and the commune is an obligor with no labour role (see RB2, RB4). Prior (capital-provider before 1433, shared after) falsified on its second phase: the commune never shares the loss.

Loss from the price of Monte credits. PHASE 1, 1425 to August 1446: the commune bore it alone; it funded dowries against credits 'but it promised investors cash, regardless of the discount market rates' (Molho 46). The value for that phase is third-party, taking the commune as the outside party of MC1. PHASE 2, from 18 August 1446, when dowries were first paid in credits issued at a discount of 18 percent and redeemed at 16 percent (Molho 47): claimants carried part. Lorenzo Corbinelli realised 952 florins of a 1,000-florin dowry in 1448 (Molho 47). It became the rule from 1472, two-thirds in credits at 22 percent (Molho 66), and from 1475, one-fifth in cash (Molho 68), with an October 1478 measure compensating claimants for the slide in prices and the November 1478 inscription of 80 percent at face value at 7 percent (Molho 68-69). The cell takes shared, the value of the longer phase. A split at 18 August 1446 (the first instance) or 21 May 1472 (when it became the rule) was proposed and REJECTED BY MS RULING 2026-10-15: one cell, resting on a locator defect, with the change episodic before 1472 (Molho 45); both phases are kept in this note instead. LOCATOR DEFECT, flagged and not repaired: no value names a counterparty-obligor who is neither capital- nor labour-provider, and third-party in phase 1 holds only on the MC1 reading. Prior (.NR) falsified.

No advance is made to a member, so nothing secures one. The depositor's advance to the commune is secured by nothing the sources name beyond the enactment's direction to pay 'de quacunque pecunia' (PR 114; Molho 31 n. 16), which is no pledge. The security the sources do describe secures a different obligation: the husband's duty to restore the dowry to his wife. It took the form of guarantors under the confessio dotis (Kirshner 2015, 102-108) and, under a law of 1441, 'security in Monte credits or real property equal in value to the Monte dowry' where the officials acted in place of the bride's father (Kirshner 2015, 112). That is dotal law between spouses, not the pool's allocation of loss; coding it would give mixed (surety and real-estate) on the wrong obligation. Flagged for MS. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (.NR) held.

Inapplicable on the locator: RB4 is located on the labour-supplying party, and this form has none. RECORDED FOR MS, NOT CODED: if the locator were read to admit the commune as the obligor whose duty to pay is extinguished when the 'venture', the girl, is lost, the value would be 1 from 23 February 1424/5 to 23 April 1433 (the whole deposit reverts; Molho 1994, 30) and P thereafter (the gain is extinguished, the principal repaid; Molho 1994, 34), with the reversion of 1434-1436 and the noncitizen reversions as variants. That is a dated change and would be a split. MS RULING 2026-10-15: locator not widened; the missing obligor locator is recorded as a vocabulary defect, to wait for a second form that needs it. Prior (.NA, medium) held.

A STRUCTURAL HALF. Priced before the event: each term carries a fixed deposit-to-dowry ratio (Kirshner and Molho 1978, 409, Table 1), and the commune set its terms with death in view. A provision of February 1462/3 stated that the longest term, 'per cagione della morte', was of 'greater utility' to the Fund (Molho 55); premiums for noncitizens were raised by 20 to 30 percent (Molho 111). Not priced on the peril of the individual girl: no rate varies with her age or health; 'Neither the legislation's enactment nor any of the subsequent laws governing the Dowry Fund refers to the interest rates promised to investors' (Molho 31); and the commune acted 'in the absence of actuarial tables' (Molho 45). Under the vocabulary's coding rule a premium inferred from yields is analyst-imposed, and so is this cell. No split. One witness: every work cited here is by Kirshner, by Molho, or by co-authors working with them from the fund's own registers, so their agreement is not corroboration. Prior (P, low) held.
